history.summary: Jyotiba temple stands at 3124 ft on Jyotiba Dongar near Wadi Ratnagiri, 18 km northwest of Kolhapur. The original Kedareshwar temple was established by Navaji Sayaji (Kedar Baba) of Kival near Karad; Ranoji Shinde replaced it with the present temple in 1730. A second Kedareshwar temple was built by Daulatrao Shinde in 1808 and a Ramling temple by Malji Nilam Panhalkar around 1780. The shrines (55 x 37 x 77 ft for the main temple) were built by Kedar craftsmen in Hemadpanti style using black basalt. Jyotiba is worshipped as the combined embodiment of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, born to Vimalmbuja (wife of sage Pougand); legend says he killed the demons Ratnasura and Raktabhoja and aided Mahalakshmi in her battle with the demons, then settled on this hill. Tradition says pilgrims should first visit the Mahalakshmi temple in Kolhapur. The fair season coats the whole complex pink with gulal.

town_description: Wadi Ratnagiri is a village in Panhala taluka of Kolhapur district, about 18 km northwest of Kolhapur city, set on the forested Jyotiba hill (3124 ft). The village exists largely around the Jyotiba pilgrimage, and the Panhala fort area is nearby. NOTE: CSV town 'Kolhapur' corrected to Wadi Ratnagiri (Jyotiba Dongar).
